note: Rule set maintained by GIS application security. Changes go through GIS-STD-014 change control; the ruleset revision is quoted in every Checkmarx report. Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions applied per line. A rule with commentedSeverity fires at that lower severity when the match is inside a comment, because a commented out strict-ssl=false is still a strict-ssl=false waiting to happen.

rules.name: Angular sanitizer bypass
rules.description: DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrust* marks a value as safe and disables Angular's contextual output encoding for it. Content from a CMS, a BFF or a translation file is still untrusted input. GIS-STD-014 section 4 requires a documented exception with an expiry for every call site.
rules.remediation: Render through Angular's default sanitisation, or move the trust decision server side and serve a pre-sanitised fragment with an integrity hash. If the bypass stays, record the GIS exception id in a comment on the call site and in checkmarx.yml suppressions.

rules.name: innerHTML binding
rules.description: innerHTML bindings are sanitised by Angular unless the value has been marked trusted, but the sanitiser strips rather than encodes and the result is rarely what the author meant. Medium because the sanitiser is in the way; High if combined with CX-ANG-001.
rules.remediation: Prefer text interpolation. Where HTML is required, use a component that renders a constrained model instead of a string.

rules.name: Direct DOM access via ElementRef
rules.description: Writing markup through ElementRef.nativeElement bypasses the template compiler and the sanitiser.
rules.remediation: Use Renderer2 or a template binding.

rules.name: Hard coded credential
rules.description: A literal that looks like a credential assigned to a credential shaped name. Secrets belong in Vault and are rendered at deploy time by the Vault agent. Placeholders must use the CHANGEME-<purpose> form so this rule does not fire.
rules.remediation: Move the value to Vault under the service's path, reference it through vault-agent.hcl and rotate it, because it is now in git history.

rules.name: Private key material in source
rules.description: A PEM private key block. Even test keys end up trusted by someone.
rules.remediation: Remove, rotate, and generate test keys at test time.

rules.name: TLS verification disabled for npm
rules.description: strict-ssl=false makes npm accept any certificate from the registry, which turns a package install into a supply chain attack surface. A commented out copy is reported at Medium because it is one uncomment away from active and it tells an attacker exactly what to try.
rules.remediation: Delete the line. If the build agent does not trust the internal CA, fix the agent image (TOOL project) rather than the client.

rules.name: Registry credentials in npmrc
rules.description: An npm auth token committed in an .npmrc.
rules.remediation: Tokens are written by the pipeline's Registry login stage from Jenkins credentials and deleted afterwards. Revoke this one.

rules.name: Dynamic code execution
rules.description: eval, new Function and string arguments to setTimeout execute arbitrary code and defeat the Content Security Policy's script-src.
rules.remediation: Replace with a parser or a lookup table. If a vendor script needs unsafe-eval the CSP exception must go through GIS.

rules.name: Certificate validation disabled
rules.description: TLS server certificate validation has been turned off. This is the single most common finding in the CSWT estate and the one that the 2024 penetration test led with.
rules.remediation: Trust the internal CA bundle from the agent or base image (/etc/pki/ca-trust) instead.

rules.name: Weak cryptographic primitive
rules.description: MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, ECB mode or java.util.Random used where the surrounding code looks security relevant.
rules.remediation: SHA-256 or better; AES-GCM; SecureRandom or crypto.randomBytes. If the hash is for a cache key say so in a comment on the line and the rule will stand down.

rules.name: Sensitive data in log statement
rules.description: A log call whose arguments name a credential, card number, SSN or account number. GIS-STD-014 section 9: no PII, PAN or tokens in logs; account numbers masked to the last four.
rules.remediation: Log the masked form or an identifier. Splunk retention is 13 months and the log index is readable by two hundred people.

rules.name: Permissive CORS
rules.description: A wildcard CORS origin on an authenticated API.
rules.remediation: List the Meridian origins explicitly; the BFF only serves the front ends in PORTS.md and their production hostnames.

rules.name: CSRF protection disabled
rules.description: Framework CSRF protection turned off. Acceptable only for token authenticated stateless APIs, and the line has to say so.
rules.remediation: Re-enable, or add the stateless justification on the same line.

rules.name: Cookie without security attributes
rules.description: A cookie written without HttpOnly and Secure.
rules.remediation: Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict. Session material never goes in a cookie the front end can read.

rules.name: SQL built by string concatenation
rules.description: A SQL statement assembled from string parts.
rules.remediation: Bind parameters. JPA named parameters, PreparedStatement, or the query builder.

rules.name: Container runs as root
rules.description: An explicit USER root in a Dockerfile. OpenShift's restricted SCC will refuse to run it anyway, and then someone asks for anyuid.
rules.remediation: Use the unprivileged base image (registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/nginx-122 or the JDK runtime image) and USER 1001.

rules.name: Unpinned or public base image
rules.category: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
rules.description: Base image pulled from outside the approved Red Hat and internal registries, or with the latest tag. DEPENDENCY_POLICY.md section 3.
rules.remediation: Pull through registry.meridian.internal/redhat-proxy or use the UBI images.

rules.name: Debug artefact left in code
rules.description: debugger statements and console output in application code. Informational; the Sonar gate counts them as code smells.
rules.remediation: Remove, or route through the telemetry service.

rules.name: Security TODO
rules.description: A TODO that mentions a security concern. These are read by the auditors before they are read by the team.
rules.remediation: Raise the GIS ticket and put the key in the comment, or do the thing.

rules.name: Content Security Policy weakened
rules.category: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers
rules.description: unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval in script-src, or a wildcard source. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is tolerated for Angular Material until the nonce work (GIS-2410) lands.
rules.remediation: Move inline scripts into bundles; vendor scripts get their origin allow-listed individually.
